A Mbuti woman is constructing a wooden frame to create a shelter in the Ituri Forest. She has a short handled knife tucked into a belt tied around her waist. Nearby, a man is seated watching another woman pick up a decorated pot.
A Mbuti man carrying a large fishing net bundled up over one shoulder for fishing on the Epulu River in the Ituri Forest.
A seated Mbuti man is playing on a hide drum with a beater.
Side portrait of a Mbuti man wearing an impressive head piece made from the fur and tail of a spotted cat (probably a Giant Genet) and white and black feathers.

Studio group by W. Downey & Co. of six Congolese 'pygmies' brought to England in 1905-1907 by James Jonathan Harrison, and exhibited in a number of locations. The group also visited the Oxford University Museum of Natural History and the Pitt Rivers Museum, where they had several portraits drawn of them (1944.1.4-6) and gave four arrows to Prof. Arthur Thomson (1936.42.1-4).
A Mbuti man, wearing a fur and feather headdress, and Robin Leech, carrying a butterfly net, standing side by side to demonstrate the difference in height between the two.
Portrait of a Mbuti man demonstrating the use of a bow and arrow. The arrows are fletched with feathers, and have iron leaf-shaped points.
Portrait of a Mbuti man sat on top of two crossed sticks. Behind him is a plant leaf structure with someone sat inside.
A Mbuti woman is weaving plant leaves through a wooden frame to create a shelter. She has a short handled knife tucked into a belt tied  around her waist.
A seated Mbuti woman, with black paint marks on her face, is staining prepared barkcloth with her fingers.
A group of Mbuti women, wearing barkcloth loin cloths, are dancing in a gathering near Camp Putnam in the Ituri Forest.

A group of dancing Mbuti men wearing barkcloth loin cloths in a gathering near Camp Putnam in the Ituri Forest. One of the men is wearing an imposing black mask with a toothy grin, white eyes and a fringe of straw, and he is supporting it from a protruding base.
A dancing Mbuti man wearing an imposing black mask with a toothy grin, white eyes and a fringe of straw, and he is supporting it from a protruding base.
A Mbuti woman is getting her face painted with a black dye in a series of geometric lines.

Anne Putnam showing four Mbuti men a book inside her home at Camp Putnam. Anne, along with her anthropologist husband Patrick, established a camp on the edge of the Ituri Forest to document the Mbuti people.
Portrait of a seated Mbuti woman with black paint marks on her chest and legs. Around her neck is an orange beaded necklace

A seated Mbuti woman, with black paint marks on her face is scraping a piece of wood against a wooden surface. A white bowl with liquid is sat next to her and a piece of barkcloth is laid out behind her.
A group of Mbuti women and children, one wearing a woven cap with a feather plume, are dancing in a gathering near Camp Putnam in the Ituri Forest.
A Mbuti woman is adding plant leaves to a wooden framed shelter in the Ituri Forest. She has a short handled knife tucked into a belt tied around her waist.
A Mbuti person is weaving plant leaves through a wooden frame to create a shelter. They are wearing a barkcloth loin cloth and a pendant necklace.
A Mbuti man beating bark with a wooden beater against a log to make barkcloth.

Two Mbuti women and a young child. One of the women has face and chest paint decoration made up of a series of criss-crossing lines and curves. The child has geometric face decoration, and is wearing a yellow beaded necklace.
